elements.name: The outlet

elements.label: Outlet Name
elements.hint: What a customer picking a branch will see. Translatable, so use the locale switcher above to add other languages

elements.label: Collection Address
elements.placeholder: e.g. 12 Jalan Telawi, Bangsar, 59100 Kuala Lumpur
elements.hint: Shown to a customer collecting from here. Leave empty to fall back to the footer address

elements.label: Phone
elements.hint: Shown with the collection address. Include the country code so a customer can tap to call from a phone

elements.label: Timezone
elements.hint: Used when this branch keeps opening hours of its own (Service Hours entries naming this branch): those are judged on this clock, so a 09:00 opening is 09:00 here whatever the season. Leave empty — or leave the branch without its own hours — and the shop's timezone under Settings applies, exactly as before

elements.subtitle: Who this branch is and how to reach it. The name is what a customer sees when they choose where to collect from, so use the name locals use — the district or mall, not the company's internal branch code.

elements.name: What is exclusive to this branch
elements.subtitle: Every branch serves the whole menu. Listed here are the dishes exclusive to THIS branch and hidden from the others — a regional special, or something only this kitchen can make. Most branches list nothing, which is correct. This is a read-out, not a control: exclusivity belongs to the dish and is set on the dish, under Store → Products → the dish → Availability → Exclusive To Branches.

elements.name: How it takes orders

elements.label: Offers Collection
elements.hint: Customers may choose to collect from here. Switched off, Collection is not offered to a customer who picks this branch

elements.label: Offers Delivery
elements.hint: This outlet delivers to its own zones. Switched off, Delivery is not offered to a customer who picks this branch

elements.label: This Branch Delivers With Its Own Riders
elements.hint: Leave this off if a courier delivers for this branch — then your Shipping zones decide how far it reaches, exactly as before. Turn it on and this branch serves a circle around its own address, and you set how wide below. You can mix the two: one branch on its own riders, another on a courier

elements.label: How Far Your Riders Go (km)
elements.hint: Measured in a straight line from this branch's own coordinates, so fill in Latitude and Longitude below or the circle cannot be drawn and this branch will refuse nothing. A delivery outside every own-rider branch's circle is turned away at checkout with the distance named, so the customer knows whether they are just outside. Leave empty and this branch refuses nothing

elements.label: Default Outlet
elements.hint: The branch used for a customer who has not chosen one. Setting this here clears it from whichever outlet held it before

elements.subtitle: Whether customers can collect from here, have it delivered from here, or both. These decide which doors the customer is shown once they pick this branch, so a branch with neither is left out of the branch list altogether — it never becomes a choice rather than becoming a dead end. Leave at least one on. Dine in is the third door and it is set below, with the dining room it belongs to.

elements.name: The dining room
elements.subtitle: Whether people eat in at THIS branch, and which tables they sit at. It starts OFF: a branch offers dining only once you switch it on here, even where Themes → Saffron → Restaurant → Offer Dine In is already on, and its tables are only reached while it is on. On, a customer who picks this branch is offered Dine in beside Collection and Delivery and is asked which table — as long as that shop-wide Offer Dine In is on and this branch offers Collection above, because a diner is recorded as collecting: they need no address and pay no delivery fee.

elements.label: Tables
elements.hint: Only reached while Offers Dine In is on. Leave it empty and the branch falls back to the shop-wide table count under Themes → Saffron → Restaurant, which gives every branch the same room — fine for one restaurant, wrong the moment two of them differ

create.title: Add Table
create.subtitle: Name it exactly as your staff say it out loud — this is what prints on the kitchen ticket.

elements.label: Table
elements.hint: Not translatable on purpose: one table, one name. If the kitchen and the customer called it different things the food would go to the wrong room

elements.label: Status
elements.hint: Out of service stops it being offered without deleting it

elements.label: Seats
elements.hint: How many people it holds. A larger party is not offered this table, and is refused if it asks for one anyway. Leave it empty and the table fits any party

elements.label: Display Order
elements.hint: Lower first. Leave empty and it falls to the end

elements.name: Where it is

elements.label: Latitude
elements.hint: Between -90 and 90. Find it by right-clicking the branch in Google Maps and copying the first number. Required when this branch delivers with its own riders — the circle is measured from here

elements.label: Longitude
elements.hint: Between -180 and 180. The second of the two numbers Google Maps copies

elements.subtitle: Where this branch sits on the map. These are read when the branch delivers with its own riders: the circle it serves is measured from this point, so a branch with the switch on and no coordinates draws no circle and turns nobody away. A delivery zone under Shipping still carries its own centre point typed on the zone — that is a separate thing, and it is what prices the delivery.

elements.label: Slug
elements.placeholder: Leave empty and it is made from the name
elements.hint: Used in links and kept unique automatically

elements.label: Status
elements.hint: Inactive hides the branch from customers immediately but keeps it, and its orders, intact

elements.label: Display Order
elements.hint: Lower sorts first, in the admin list and the customer's branch picker
